_comment: MCP resource spec for #2 Strategy Pressure-Tester. Phase 2 .mcpb bundle target. The lenny-pressure-test skill in this repo is the engine reference. Draft 2026-05-17 — MCP Apps spec (Jan 2026) is young; owner to validate before locking.

resource.name: Strategy Pressure-Tester
resource.description: Paste a strategy doc, PRD, or roadmap. Returns the five strongest objections a smart skeptic would raise (Rumelt-style diagnosis, missing tradeoffs, untested assumptions, six-month stress scenario), each anchored to the Lenny corpus.

tools.name: strategy_classify
tools.description: Deterministic. Classifies the input as strategy / roadmap / prd / mixed so downstream critique uses the right vocabulary.

signals.description: Short reasons for the classification (e.g., 'no named challenge', 'features-by-quarter pattern').

tools.name: strategy_critique
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Runs the four-pass critique (Rumelt diagnosis, missing tradeoffs, untested assumptions, six-month stress scenario) and returns five objection cards.

tools.name: strategy_rehearse
tools.description: LLM-narrated. Multi-turn rehearsal of the counter to one chosen objection. Skeptic pushes back; user argues; ends with the strategy variant that survives.

tools.name: strategy_calibration
tools.description: MCP-only (stateful). Compares the current critique against the prior critique for the same user. Surfaces assumptions that resolved, tradeoffs the user actually made, and the next-quarter stress scenario.
tools._phase_note: Web version does not expose this tool. Calibration requires persisted prior critiques, which is .mcpb data-dir scope.

_open_questions: Validate ui:// URI scheme against current MCP Apps spec.
Confirm tool composition pattern (classify → critique → rehearse) matches MCP-Apps recommended flow.
Decide whether strategy_text should be stored hashed for calibration, or only the critique summary. Privacy posture in plan says default-off retention.
Engine sharing: should strategy_critique tool import directly from lenny-pressure-test skill, or duplicate the corpus-routing logic for .mcpb portability?
_proposed_answers: Confirmed valid. The Jan 2026 MCP Apps spec uses ui:// for embedded UI resources. 'ui://working-from-lenny/pressure-test' matches the required pattern.

Yes. The Jan 2026 spec recommends composable, separable tools within a single resource. The three-step flow (classify then critique then rehearse) maps cleanly to this pattern: the host can invoke each step independently or chain them, passing doc_type from strategy_classify into strategy_critique as a parameter. Tool chaining with explicit handoff values (not implicit session state) is the recommended flow.

Store the critique summary only, not the full strategy text. Strategy docs can contain confidential roadmaps; full-text retention is the highest-risk item. The calibration value comes from tracking which objection labels resolved and which the user rehearsed, not from replaying the original text. Recommended: store critique ID, timestamp, the five objection labels (not full text), and chosen_objection_index. Hash the strategy text for deduplication if needed; do not store plaintext. Default off per the plan's privacy posture; enabled via data-retention capability in the bundle manifest.

Duplicate the corpus-routing logic for .mcpb portability. The Jan 2026 .mcpb bundle format is self-contained; the host cannot be expected to install the lenny-pressure-test skill as a dependency. Bundle the relevant corpus chunks and routing logic directly. If the skill is updated, a bundle refresh is the update path. Portability over DRY is the right tradeoff for Phase 2. Flag the duplication with a comment in the bundle so a Phase 3 refactor can consolidate if the spec adds inter-bundle references.
